subject.title: [Feature]: Skill lifecycle management — auto-optimization on failure + usage-based retirement

question: Should OpenClaw add core-owned skill lifecycle state/config for failure/performance optimization and retirement, or keep this as plugin/ClawHub work backed by narrower core diagnostics and hook seams?
rationale: The remaining behavior is not a narrow bug fix: it changes how OpenClaw derives durable skill edits from execution history, stores usage metrics, and hides or deletes user-visible skills.

options.title: Design a narrow core seam first
options.body: Define the minimal core events, metrics, storage owner, and Skill Workshop proposal semantics, then let core or plugins build lifecycle policy on top of that seam.

options.title: Route to plugin/ClawHub
options.body: Keep core limited to current skill.used diagnostics and tool hooks, and ask for a plugin/ClawHub package unless a concrete missing API is identified.

options.title: Accept the full core feature
options.body: Implement the proposed config, CLI/UI, metrics store, optimization proposals, archive, and retirement policy in core, accepting the larger compatibility and UX surface.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow core seam first
recommendation.body: Define the minimal core events, metrics, storage owner, and Skill Workshop proposal semantics, then let core or plugins build lifecycle policy on top of that seam.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter authored the default suggestion-tier product change that closed the broader related issue and is tied to adjacent Skill Workshop product wording decisions.
